target_customer: Households in California first (then the US), buying a home robot for laundry and tidying
problem: Household chores such as folding laundry and tidying consume time and no affordable general purpose home robot existed.
business_model: Hardware sales ($7,999 upfront or $449 per month for Isaac 1 per press) with remote operation support by Weave for tasks the robot cannot yet do

founders.name: Kaan Dogrusoz
prior_employers: Apple (manager in ML Robotics research, staff ML researcher, lead embedded engineer on iPhone)
founders.background_notes: From the YC company page, which says he shipped Double Tap on Apple Watch

founders.name: Evan Wineland
founders.background_notes: Friends and roommates with Dogrusoz since 2015 per the YC page

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous manipulation of deformable objects such as laundry in homes is research grade, and the company relies on remote operation for tasks the robot cannot do. It also needs hardware manufacturing.

defensibility.rationale: Hard robotics and manipulation data take time to replicate, but well funded humanoid companies target the same market.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: 1X, Figure and Tesla pursued home robots; press in July 2026 names 1X Neo at about $20,000, Tesla Optimus and Figure as rivals to Isaac 1. No acquisition or copying of Weave found.

market_need_then: Laundry and chores are universal pain points, and demand was shown by pre-orders: YC page says customers could reserve Isaac for $1,000. Dated 2024 demand evidence beyond that was not found.

identity.mascot_or_character: The robot is named Isaac (origin of the name not stated); body colors named Sage and Terracotta
identity.visual_style: soft robot with two orange claws instead of fingers per press
identity.voice_and_tone: short and upbeat, tagline practical and delightful robots, shipping today

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage of Isaac 0 and Isaac 1 across robotics and general tech outlets (Automate.org, The Next Web, designboom, Business Insider Japan)

brand_strength.rationale: A named, friendly product character and broad press coverage in 2026, but the product name overlaps with NVIDIA Isaac and the company name is generic.

pivots.from: General home robot (Isaac) promised for fall 2025
pivots.to: Stationary laundry folding robot Isaac 0 shipping first, then mobile Isaac 1
pivots.why: Not stated by a source; shipping dates moved from fall 2025 to Isaac 0 in February 2026 and Isaac 1 in fall 2026

outcome_analysis: Weave is active and shipping a laundry folding robot in California since early 2026, with a mobile Isaac 1 announced in July 2026 and a goal of 1,000 homes by the end of 2027. The founders are former Apple robotics and AI staff. Original shipping targets slipped, and no priced institutional round was found, so funding and scaling remain the key risks.
notes: Funding: trackers (Sacra, Seedtable, VCBacked, Caplight) report about $500K pre-seed or seed in September to November 2024 with Y Combinator, Pioneer Fund, Collide Capital, Nexus and others; round label, date and investors conflict across aggregators and no primary source was opened, so no round is recorded. Team size shows 26 in the directory and about 10 in one early 2026 listing. Competitor search returned only 2025 and 2026 coverage, so the list is empty. Shipping facts (Isaac 0 February 2026, Isaac 1 price and dates) come from search snippets and The Next Web. Completeness pass: a 500K round rests on trackers only (Sacra says pre-seed October 2024; Neuronfeed says seed September 2024; Seedtable lists a conflicting date). Label, date and investor list conflict, so treat as one uncertain round.
